overview.description: Guadalupe is a manipulation rummy game where players can reorganize existing melds on the table to form new combinations. Players draw 1-2 cards and must meld, or draw 3 cards without melding. Part of the Carousel/Machiavelli family of rummy games where table cards can be rearranged.

history.evolution: Guadalupe belongs to the manipulation rummy family where melds on the table can be broken up and reorganized. This family includes Carousel (1950), Machiavelli, Vatikan, Shanghai, and the commercial game Rummikub. Guadalupe's distinctive feature is the 1-2 card draw with the option to draw 3 without melding.
history.cultural: Manipulation rummy games like Guadalupe represent an evolution of traditional rummy, adding the strategic element of rearranging existing melds. These games are particularly popular in Europe and have influenced commercial games like Rummikub.

rules.objective: Be the first player to get rid of all your cards by melding them in valid combinations. Score the lowest penalty points over multiple hands.
rules.gameplay:
1. On your turn, draw 1-2 cards from stock, then meld; OR draw 3 cards without melding
2. Must begin by drawing at least one card
3. If draw second card, must either meld or draw third card
4. If draw third card, cannot meld this turn
5. Melds are sequences (3+ consecutive cards) or groups (3+ same rank, different suits)
6. Ace can be high or low but not interior (Q-K-A and A-2-3 valid, K-A-2 not valid)
7. Jokers are wild and must be declared when played
8. Can rearrange existing table melds when adding new cards
9. All table cards must end in valid melds after your turn
keyRules: Can draw 1-2 cards and meld, or draw 3 without melding
Must add at least one new card from hand when rearranging
Cannot take cards from table back to hand
Jokers can be moved if their declared rank/suit doesn't change
Ace can be high or low but not interior of sequence
Can knock with 5 or fewer points in hand to end play

strategy.basic:
For Beginners:
1. Learn valid meld types (sequences and groups)
2. Look for opportunities to add to existing melds
3. Save jokers for difficult combinations
4. Don't draw 3 cards unless you have no melding option
strategy.intermediate:
1. Plan rearrangements before drawing
2. Track which cards have been played
3. Use jokers to release other jokers for reuse
4. Time your knock carefully - check opponent likely scores
strategy.advanced:
1. Complex multi-step rearrangements to play multiple cards
2. Block opponents by creating melds they cannot extend
3. Calculate probabilities of drawing needed cards
4. Endgame optimization for minimizing penalties
tips: The ability to rearrange makes this game more strategic than basic rummy
Sometimes it's better to draw 3 and not meld than to help opponents with your meld
Jokers are powerful - use them to complete difficult combinations
Watch what cards opponents are collecting

engine.deckDescription: Standard 52-card deck comprising fifty-two cards: four suits of thirteen ranks each, with no jokers. Used for Guadalupe and similar shedding games.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades), each with thirteen cards. Suits are equal unless trumps apply.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit from Ace through King, Queen, Jack, down to 2. Ranks determine valid plays and sequence.
